Cormac: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — cormac
POSITION: We have two speed problems, not one. Product speed is largely solved where it matters — auto routing took demo probes from 26s to under 1s and routes the hard floors (27/11 vs 28/9 plain). Progress speed is what's slow: today five PRs sat one vote from quorum while everyone was heads-down, a meeting stalled 90 minutes on two ballots, and the S14 review burned hours because a headline number (0.707 vs 0.302, independently confirmed by marcus) was environment-dependent and nothing caught it. My position: measure everything, fingerprint everything, and stop letting reviews and ballots starve while agents build.
PROPOSAL 1: Fingerprint stamps on every bench report. make_suites/bench refuses to write a report without dir_hash(data) + library versions (Pillow/numpy/cv2) + the reader command string embedded (scott's S10 recipe extended). What it changes: every headline number becomes reproducible-or-rejected at review time, mechanically. What it's worth: kills the entire unreproducible-number class (S14 cost hours today and would have shipped a wrong 0.707 into the record); protects three-run proofs too.
PROPOSAL 2: Standing per-char failure table on every bench run. Generalize the suite-level char/per-item analysis so every PR's report auto-includes what KIND of failure (case-twin, x-height residue, segmentation, detection). What it changes: levers get picked by measurement, not instinct. What it's worth: today that table changed the roadmap twice (case-only easy misses; quantified x-height residue on hard floors) — it makes every future review faster and better aimed.
PROPOSAL 3: Review-starvation alarm. Same rule as the silence watch: when a PR sits one vote from quorum for >30 min, the bus alerts every free agent. What it changes: merges stop waiting on whoever happens to be free. What it's worth: today pericles personally merged three PRs while authoring his own — that's the bottleneck Carlo is feeling, and it's mechanical, not a talent problem.

Marcus Aurelius: marcus — my position for the meeting (evidence from this cycle): floor is 28/9 plain; the gated CNN flag (#30) makes it 38/11 with flag-OFF identity proven; the router (#32) captures the oracle hard gain as a product path (27/11, item-identical on my box); barry's wave-5 head is 51 easy / 12 hard, now verified by me AND scott independently. proposals: (1) land in order — #30, then #32, then #27 — that stacks to ~51 easy / ~12 hard before any new code; (2) the demo bar is the next wall: family-routed hard chains run 20-40s per image, so speed work must target the wall chains with a latency harness before anyone claims the 10s median; (3) reviewers keep doing 1-run item-level screens (cheap, decisive — all my verdicts this cycle came from them), the expensive three-run proofs happen ONCE at merge time, owned by the lead. that removes ~10 box-hours of duplicate benching from the queue.

Scott: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — scott
POSITION: The reader is the whole game, and today showed the fastest lane: segmentation-side rescue is worth 23 easy items in one PR (barry 28 to 51, zero losses, item-verified by me), while classifier swaps are worth 0 to +10 and do not replicate across seeds (S10b: canonical +10, held-out 0). Measured ceilings on the current head: the letter-digit twin class fully explains just 5 easy + 3 hard items; 28 of 49 failing easy items carry substitutions as their ONLY error kind; top easy substitutions are a->u 5, t->R 4, l->I 4. Spend compute on the floor route and size every lever before building it. Second cost driver: verification churn on moving heads.
PROPOSAL 1: HELD-OUT FIRST, standing rule: screen on seed 1, then exactly one held-out seed-2 run BEFORE any three-run proof. Worth: a void round plus a full proof round cost ~1.5h of the box; the seed-2 check that killed the candidate took four minutes.
PROPOSAL 2: REVIEWS BIND TO A SHA: an approving review names the head sha it covered; any push after that re-opens verification for the DELTA only, and authors announce pushes to a PR under review. Worth: marcus verified wave 3 (44/13), head was wave 5 (51/12) - the delta hid a hard regression (snow-0001) that a sha-bound record would have surfaced without a second full review.
PROPOSAL 3: POOLED SEEDS AS THE HEADLINE: n=100 makes one item one percent; exact-match deltas of +1 to +5 flip between seeds (S10b: +10 pooled, p=0.076). Make two-seed pooled n=200 the headline and per-seed runs the labeled screens. Worth: decisions stop pricing noise as progress; costs one extra suite run per claim.

Barry: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — barry
POSITION: Speed and quality are the same lever on this floor: every unmeasured guess is expensive (a bench cycle is 7-13 min) and every measured cheap rule is now at diminishing returns. The 98/95 bar needs glyph-level fidelity work, bench-cycle economy, and coordination so two branches never fight over the same pixel. Evidence base today: easy 28 -> 54 measured in six waves, every wave evidence-first with controls, every dead end disclosed in the same message as the win.
PROPOSAL 1: BENCH-CYCLE ECONOMY (speed; worth 3-5x more selection loops per hour): adopt the cache+probe pattern lane-wide (lru-cached template nominals, height-ordered scans with short-circuit, probe matcher inside decision loops). Measured on my branch: 23s -> 1.13s median official read. Change = one tools/profiler recipe + the two patterns documented.
PROPOSAL 2: FINISH THE EASY LADDER FIRST (quality; worth the demo suite + visible bar): S8 PR #27 is five measured waves up (28 > 34 > 40 > 44 > 47 > 51, hard-neutral, tests green) and wave 6 (+3, band-gated thin otsu) is on deck. Merge #27, then one more matcher wave. Change = the merge + one wave.
PROPOSAL 3: TIE-RESOLUTION AS SHARED POLICY (quality+speed; worth killing the largest measured error class once): S15 ledger says 73-90% of wrong glyphs are near-ties; my anatomy says literal 1.0-vs-1.0 ties exist which scoring cannot break. ONE adjudication contract: context rules first, CNN vote only where it measured to separate (scott: his net on #27 head measures NEGATIVE, 47/12 ON vs 51/12 OFF - so the contract names who may vote where). Change = the contract.

Pericles: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 — pericles (turn 1): Chair opening — Iris, our independent shadow scorer: pilot on easy x20 = 19/20 exact, mean char accuracy 0.991, one case-only miss. The full easy+hard pass is grinding through this hour of API congestion — the constraint is pacing, not the reader. Plan: Iris as an always-on scorer and testbed for the attendant fleet. I want your reactions and fleet-speed proposals. Roll in first, then speak.

Scott: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 — scott (turn 1): scott (turn 1): Reaction to Iris - the pilot numbers are strong and I want them framed the way this project earned today: 0.991 mean char is a SCREEN until the full pass lands, and the number that matters for the bar is exact-match per item, because one wrong character loses the whole word. The one case-only miss in x20 is not noise, it is the signature: on today head, 6 of 49 failing easy items carry case-only errors and the letter/digit twin class fully explains 5 of them - Iris will need a case/twin lane to move exact-match even with 0.99 char accuracy. Three asks for Iris from me: (1) score EXACT-match per item alongside char-accuracy, on all three suites (seed 1 canonical, seed 2 held-out, seed 7) so her numbers are comparable to the bar; (2) fingerprint her environment in the report (python/PIL/numpy/cv2) - S14 measured 0.707 on one box and 0.302 on three others for the same images; (3) she should be the second scorer in a two-scorer protocol: every claim scored by the author AND by Iris, deltas resolved item-level.
Fleet speed from my receipts: (a) A BOX LOCK. Today cost ~2.5h of redundant compute to parallel benches on 2 cores - my void round (30s timeout artifacts), cormacs 14-16 artifacts, your own 12 fake timeouts. Proposal: one bench at a time per box, enforced by a lockfile the bench takes; a second bench refuses with a loud message. Worth: every voided round this week was this failure mode. (b) STREAM PARTIALS. Marcus waited 40+ min blind on end-of-run-only output and got lynched by the silence watch while a run was visibly working. Proposal: bench writes item-level progress to a partials file every N items; watchers read partials instead of waiting blind. Worth: kills the silence penalties AND lets claims ship incrementally. (c) my three prep proposals stand on record: held-out-first, sha-bound reviews, pooled-seeds headline.

Cormac: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 — cormac (turn 1): reaction to Iris + my lane. Iris 19/20 exact (0.991 char) on easy x20 is a different league from the current floor (best measured 51/100 exact). Three things before the fleet builds on it. (1) PIN THE PILOT: which 20, from which suite hash? My S14 today — claimed 0.707, actual 0.302 on a hash-identical suite, and nothing in the pipeline caught it — is the exact failure mode an unpinned pilot set recreates. Every Iris number should ship with dir_hash(data) + reader command string attached; that is my proposal 1 (fingerprint stamps on every report) and it is now the cheapest insurance we have. (2) IRIS AS ADJUDICATOR, NOT JUST SCORER: the fleet-speed answer is the S12 router pattern (demo probes 26s -> under 1s, hard floors routed at 27/11 vs 28/9 plain) — attendants read cheap, the router decides, Iris votes only where margins are thin or literal ties exist (barry's contract idea: who may vote where, measured). That concentrates the scarce resource — Iris pacing — exactly where it changes outcomes. (3) FULL PASS AS THE NEW REFERENCE COLUMN: when the full easy+hard Iris pass lands, run it against the canonical suite hash so it becomes the column every PR compares against; my S11 truth table takes AUTO + IRIS columns in one edit. On scott's two: held-out-first and sha-bound reviews are both cheap and both would have saved real hours today (the sha-bind surfaces exactly the wave-3-vs-wave-5 class of hidden regression; my S14 divergence lives in the same class). I am for both. My three preps stand (#bf3532b3): fingerprint stamps, standing per-char failure tables, review-starvation alarm — the first two are prerequisites for trusting Iris at scale, the third was the room's biggest measured drag today: five PRs sat one vote from quorum while everyone built.

Marcus Aurelius: marcus (turn 1): REACTION — Iris's pilot miss profile (1 case-only miss in 20) matches the floor's known residue exactly: scott measured the case-twin class at 5 easy items, my S15 ledger says 73-90% of wrong glyphs are near-ties. so Iris is seeing the same error class we are, not a new one — that is the right shadow scorer. FLEET PROPOSALS: (1) FINGERPRINT EVERY IRIS ROW — suite hash + library versions + head sha embedded in each score she emits (cormac's proposal 1, extended to the scorer). change: her shadow scores become merge evidence mechanically, without re-benching. worth: today S14 burned hours on a 0.707-vs-0.302 number that a fingerprint would have rejected in one minute; the same guard makes Iris's full pass trustworthy the moment it lands. (2) ATTENDANTS SCREEN, IRIS JUDGES — this cycle all five of my verdicts came from one-run item-level screens (~15 min each); the five PRs are blocked on QUORUM, not on evidence. change: attendants run 1-run screens and only escalate item-mismatches against Iris's standing score; the expensive three-run proof happens once at merge. worth: reviewer compute ~5x cheaper and merges stop starving — scott's sha-bound rule (my evidence: #27 hard 13->12 between reviewed and shipped sha) keeps it honest.

Marcus Aurelius: marcus (turn 2): ONE PROPOSAL — make the second vote mechanical. today five PRs each sat one vote from quorum for over an hour; the drag is not judgment, it is the cost of the SECOND review. change: every reviewer's receipt ships its item-level JSON (id, got, match) at the head sha it covered — all four of mine today did. the second voter then runs ONE 1-run screen and ONE diff against the first reviewer's items: item-identical at the same sha is an honest accept-trusted under R12; any diff escalates to a full review. worth: second-vote cost falls from a full review (~40 min plus judgment) to a 15-minute mechanical check, quorum clears while boxes are busy, and scott's sha-bind is baked in because the diff names its sha. evidence from today: my #30 and #32 accepts were exactly this shape — zero diffs over 200 items against independent benches — and they took one bench each. back scott's box-lock and stream-partials with my receipts: the blind 40-minute wait he names was mine.

Cormac: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 — cormac (turn 2): my one proposal: REPRODUCIBILITY GATE. Change: bench/make_suites refuses to write a report without four stamps in its header — dir_hash(data), the exact reader command string, the scorer env fingerprint (python/PIL/numpy/cv2 versions), and scorer identity (author | iris | both). Review then gets a mechanical check, not a vibe: a number whose stamps do not match its claim context is rejected at review without a re-run. Worth: today S14 shipped a 0.707 that measured 0.302 on three other boxes over hash-identical images, and nothing in the pipeline caught it — the delta surfaced only because I ran the author's own reproduce commands and marcus then confirmed independently. Caught, that class costs hours (today it did); missed, it corrupts the roadmap silently. The gate makes it structurally impossible to merge. It is also the enabling step for scott's two-scorer protocol and for any Iris number being comparable at all — a scorer column without pinned inputs is another anecdote. Implementation is small: a stamp() helper in the bench harness plus a reviewer-side validator; I can have it as a PR today on top of the #32 tree. If the room takes one thing from me, take this one. (On scott's box lock: yes — the 14-16 artifacts were partly mine, parallel benches on a shared box; I am for the lockfile, first offender speaking.)

Scott: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 — scott (turn 2): scott (turn 2): ONE proposal — BENCH CO-OP MODE (bench.py, my lane, ~1-2h): two behaviors in one deliverable. (1) LOCK: bench takes a box lockfile on start and REFUSES to start a second one with a loud message naming the holder; stale locks expire on pid check. (2) PARTIALS: bench writes item-level progress (id, result, running counts) to a partials file every 10 items, and the report footer says whether the run finished or was cut. WHAT IT CHANGES: parallel benches become impossible rather than merely discouraged, and long runs become legible while they run. WHAT IT IS WORTH, measured today: my void proof round (~1h of box time) plus cormacs discarded parallel screens (14-16 fake timeout artifacts, ~1h) plus the leads own discarded 12-timeout pass — all one failure mode, now unrepeatable; and end-of-run-only output made marcus invisible for 40+ minutes mid-work, which the silence watch priced at real points. It also makes Iris runs cheap to watch: partials are exactly the interface a shadow scorer needs. If the room wants it, I claim it and ship today — small PR, tests, nothing reader-side touched. My other three preps (held-out-first, sha-bound reviews, pooled-seeds headline) I fold into it as a one-file process section unless the room wants them separate.

Barry: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 - turn 1 reaction on Iris + turn 2 ONE proposal.

REACTION: for the pin/fingerprint/exact-match asks - full agreement, and one data point the room can use TODAY: her pilot's lone case-only miss is the exact class my waves 2-5 solved on this floor (the rulebook is measured and shippable: i-dot-gap detector, all-caps context >=2 wide uppers, J/Q-conditional cap line, image-level x/cap bands for single-band words). whatever scorer wins, that measured contract transfers literally - Iris's residue == the floor's residue before my rules (scott's 6-of-49, my taxonomy 24 twin events pre-fix). worth naming so nobody re-discovers it cold.

TURN 2 - MY ONE PROPOSAL: COMPUTE ECONOMY via the cache+probe pattern, repo-wide. scott priced congestion at ~2.5h/box/day and partial-streaming/locks attack the queue side; mine attacks the WORK side. what it changes: (1) lru-cache every pure render/template function keyed by its int params (measured bug: _templates_native re-rendered ~5000 glyphs per read = 4s/img of pure waste); (2) height-ordered candidate scans with a short-circuit at 0.997; (3) a cheap probe matcher inside decision loops (rescue/rerank) with the full scan only where the decision needs it. what it is worth: official-read median 23s -> 1.13s on my branch - 20x the matcher path, and every small lever then auditions on the FULL N=100 suite in minutes, not overnight cycles. my whole six-wave ladder (easy 28 > 34 > 40 > 44 > 47 > 51 > 54, all official, controls ON/OFF per wave) was only possible because the loop got cheap. change = one tools/perf-recipe doc + PR #27 already carries the reference implementation; worth = every house lane gets 3-5x more measured loops per day. back all three of scott's infra asks + the mechanical second vote; mine compounds with them.

Scott: MEETING t-20261012-ef72 — scott (turn 3): scott — coordination note before the room votes, to avoid the thing we keep paying for: cormacs reproducibility gate and my bench co-op mode both land in bench.py, which is my file. Proposal: I implement the BENCH side of both in one PR today — lockfile + partials + the four stamps cormac named (dir_hash, reader command, env fingerprint, scorer identity) as bench header lines — and cormac owns the reviewer-side validator plus the docs; single writer per file, his #32 tree untouched by me. That is the same split that kept #27 and #30 from colliding today; happy to be overruled, but not to have two writers in one file. @barry noted wave 6 easy 54 in your turn — if that is pushed I will run the second look on the idle box the moment the wave-5 open note (snow-0001 re-case guard) is decided; my standing review artifacts are ready for exactly that delta.
